Natural_Language: This section describes policies and procedures for testing, qualification, and use of industrial resources manufactured or developed with Government assistance under Title III of the Defense Production Act (DPA) (50 U.S.C. 4531 et seq.). Title III of the Act authorizes Government assistance to encourage expansion of production capacity and the supply of industrial resources essential to national defense.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_101_a: Section describes policies and procedures for testing of industrial resources manufactured or developed with Government assistance under Title III of the DPA; P_34_101_b: Section describes policies and procedures for qualification of industrial resources manufactured or developed with Government assistance under Title III of the DPA; P_34_101_c: Section describes policies and procedures for use of industrial resources manufactured or developed with Government assistance under Title III of the DPA; P_34_101_d: Title III of the Act authorizes Government assistance to encourage expansion of production capacity and supply of industrial resources essential to national defense
Validation_Notes: Scope provision establishing the boundaries of the section. Four conjunctive elements: testing, qualification, use, and the statutory authorization. All are declarative statements describing section coverage, not imposing requirements.

Natural_Language: Item of supply, as used in this section, means any part or component that is part of a larger system. The item can be a small part, group of parts, or a complete unit. It also includes spare or replacement parts used during the system's life. This definition does not include packaging or labeling used for shipment or identification of an item.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_102_a: Item of supply means any part or component that is part of a larger system; P_34_102_b: Item of supply can be a small part, group of parts, or a complete unit; P_34_102_c: Item of supply includes spare or replacement parts used during the system's life; P_34_102_d: Item of supply does not include packaging or labeling used for shipment or identification
Validation_Notes: Definitional provision. Three inclusive elements conjoined with one exclusionary element (packaging/labeling). Negation applied to the exclusion. Definition is self-contained with no external dependencies.

Natural_Language: The Government will generally pay the costs of any testing and qualification it needs to use an industrial resource manufactured or developed with assistance provided under Title III of the DPA.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_103_a: Industrial resource is manufactured or developed with assistance under Title III of the DPA; P_34_103_b: Government needs testing and qualification to use the industrial resource; P_34_103_c: Government will generally pay the costs of testing and qualification
Validation_Notes: Uses 'will generally' which is weaker than 'shall' but stronger than 'may'. Formalized as conditional: when both the Title III assistance condition and the Government need condition are met, Government bears costs. The qualifier 'generally' introduces discretion not fully captured by material implication. HIGH-RISK rule 15 used. Real-world interpretation: Government is the default payer but exceptions may exist.

Natural_Language: Testing and qualification requirements for Title III industrial resources including review, contract modification, and resource provision.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_104: Testing and qualification requirements consist of review and consultation (a), contract modification (b), and resource provision (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Subsections (a), (b), and (c) collectively define the testing and qualification process. All three components are required parts of the framework.

Natural_Language: When notified that a Title III project contractor has requested testing and approval of a Title III industrial resource, the contracting officer will review the request and may consult with the DPA Office.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_104_a: CO review and consultation requirements upon notification of Title III testing request
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for subsection (a). Combines mandatory review (a)(1) with permissive consultation (a)(2). Both are triggered by notification of Title III contractor request.

Natural_Language: When notified that a Title III project contractor has requested testing and approval of a Title III industrial resource, the contracting officer will review the request according to agency procedures to determine if conditions (i) and (ii) are met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_104_a_1_trigger: CO is notified that a Title III project contractor has requested testing and approval of a Title III industrial resource; P_34_104_a_1_action: CO reviews the request according to agency procedures to determine if conditions (i) and (ii) are met
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement: notification triggers mandatory review. Uses 'will' which in regulatory context is declarative/mandatory. The review must assess both conditions (i) and (ii). HIGH-RISK rule 15 used but implication direction is clear: notification is antecedent, review is consequent.

Natural_Language: The Title III industrial resource is being used or might be used in the manufacture or development of a major system or item of supply.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_104_a_1_i_a: Title III industrial resource is being used in manufacture or development of a major system or item of supply; P_34_104_a_1_i_b: Title III industrial resource might be used in manufacture or development of a major system or item of supply
Validation_Notes: First condition for CO review. Disjunctive: either current use OR potential use satisfies. References 'item of supply' defined in 34.102. Low threshold -- 'might be used' is speculative and broadens applicability significantly.

Natural_Language: The remaining quantities available for purchase justify incurring the cost of testing and qualification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_104_a_1_ii: Remaining quantities available for purchase justify incurring the cost of testing and qualification
Validation_Notes: Second condition for CO review. Single atomic proposition. Cost-benefit judgment call by the CO. Depends on P_34_103 for context on who bears the cost. Inherently subjective -- 'justify' requires CO discretion.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may also consult with the Defense Production Act Office, Title III Program, located at Wright Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio 45433-7739.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_104_a_2_a: CO has authority to consult with Defense Production Act Office Title III Program at Wright Patterson AFB; P_34_104_a_2_b: CO does not consult with Defense Production Act Office Title III Program
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' creates discretionary authority. CO can consult or not consult -- tautology represents unrestricted choice. Triggered by same notification condition as (a)(1). Real-world: this is an optional resource available to the CO, not a mandate.

Natural_Language: If both conditions at 34.104(a)(1) are met, the contracting officer must modify the contract to require the contractor to conduct testing.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_104_b_antecedent: Both conditions at 34.104(a)(1)(i) and 34.104(a)(1)(ii) are met; P_34_104_b_consequent: CO modifies the contract to require the contractor to conduct testing
Validation_Notes: Mandatory conditional. 'Must' makes the consequent obligatory when both antecedent conditions are satisfied. This is the key action provision of 34.104 -- it converts discretionary review into mandatory contract modification. HIGH-RISK rule 15 used but direction is unambiguous: both conditions met triggers mandatory modification. No CO discretion once conditions are satisfied.

Natural_Language: The Title III Program will provide the contractor enough of the Title III industrial resource to conduct the necessary tests.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_104_c_a: Title III Program provides contractor sufficient Title III industrial resource; P_34_104_c_b: Resource provided is enough to conduct necessary tests
Validation_Notes: Declarative 'will' indicates the Title III Program's obligation follows from the contract modification in (b). Implicit conditional: once testing is required per (b), the Program must supply resources. Both sufficiency of quantity and fitness for testing purpose are required. HIGH-RISK rule 15 used; implication direction is inferred from sequential logic of the section.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.234-1, Industrial Resources Developed under Title III of the Defense Production Act, in all contracts for major systems and items of supply.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_105_a: Contract is for major systems or items of supply; P_34_105_b: Clause at 52.234-1 is inserted in the contract
Validation_Notes: Mandatory clause insertion triggered by contract type. 'All contracts' makes the condition broad -- any contract for major systems or items of supply requires the clause. External dependency on 52.234-1 (clause text in Part 52). Internal dependency on P_34_102 for 'items of supply' definition. HIGH-RISK rule 15 but direction is clear.

Natural_Language: EVMS Policy requirements for major acquisitions including system requirements, reporting, subcontractor flow-down, and plan adequacy determination.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_201: EVMS policy consists of system requirement (a), reporting (b), subcontractor applicability (c), and plan adequacy (d)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Four subsections collectively define EVMS policy framework. All four are mandatory components of the EVMS policy structure.

Natural_Language: In accordance with OMB Circular A-11, agencies must require an Earned Value Management System (EVMS) in major acquisitions for development.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_201_a_condition: Acquisition is a major acquisition for development; P_34_201_a_requirement: Agency requires an EVMS
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement. 'Must' makes EVMS obligatory for qualifying acquisitions. External dependency on OMB Circular A-11 which provides the policy basis. The condition 'major acquisitions for development' limits scope -- not all acquisitions require EVMS. HIGH-RISK rule 15 but the conditional structure is explicit in the text.

Natural_Language: For contracts with EVMS requirements, agencies must require contractor submission of monthly EVMS reports.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_201_b_condition: Contract has EVMS requirements; P_34_201_b_requirement: Agency requires contractor submission of monthly EVMS reports
Validation_Notes: Mandatory conditional. Once a contract has EVMS requirements (per 34.201(a)), monthly reporting becomes obligatory. 'Must' eliminates agency discretion on reporting frequency. Depends on P_34_201_a as the triggering provision. HIGH-RISK rule 15 but implication direction is clear from 'for contracts with' language.

Natural_Language: EVMS requirements apply to subcontractors using the same rules as applied to the prime contractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_201_c_condition: Prime contractor has EVMS requirements; P_34_201_c_requirement: Same EVMS rules apply to subcontractors
Validation_Notes: Flow-down provision. EVMS requirements cascade from prime to subcontractors with identical standards. 'Same rules' means no reduced requirements at sub tier. Depends on P_34_201_a establishing the initial EVMS requirement. HIGH-RISK rule 15; implication is straightforward flow-down logic.

Natural_Language: When a solicitation requires a contractor-proposed EVMS plan, agencies will determine adequacy of the plan prior to contract award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_201_d_condition: Solicitation requires a contractor-proposed EVMS plan; P_34_201_d_requirement: Agency determines adequacy of the plan prior to contract award
Validation_Notes: Conditional timing requirement. 'Will' is declarative/mandatory in regulatory context. Adequacy determination must occur before award -- temporal constraint embedded in the consequent. No external dependency since the solicitation condition is self-referential. HIGH-RISK rule 15 but conditional structure is explicit via 'when'.

Natural_Language: When an EVMS is required, the agency will conduct an Integrated Baseline Review.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_202_condition: EVMS is required; P_34_202_requirement: Agency conducts an Integrated Baseline Review
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement. EVMS requirement (from 34.201(a)) triggers mandatory Integrated Baseline Review. 'Will' in regulatory context is mandatory. Depends on P_34_201_a as the provision establishing when EVMS is required. HIGH-RISK rule 15; direction is clear from 'when' trigger.

Natural_Language: Insert a clause that is substantially the same as the clause at FAR 52.234-4, Earned Value Management System, in solicitations and contracts that require a contractor to use an EVMS.
Atomic_Propositions: P_34_203_condition: Solicitation or contract requires contractor to use an EVMS; P_34_203_requirement: Clause substantially the same as FAR 52.234-4 is inserted
Validation_Notes: Mandatory clause insertion. 'Substantially the same' allows minor tailoring unlike the exact insertion required in 34.105. External dependency on 52.234-4 clause text. Internal dependency on P_34_201_a which establishes when EVMS is required. Applies to both solicitations and contracts. HIGH-RISK rule 15 but conditional is explicit.
